text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced 4.6% today, recovering some ground after a brutal five-day sell-off that wiped out 13% of its value. The rebound comes as oil prices stabilized—U.S. crude holding near $100 a barrel while refineries run at a high 94.5% capacity utilization—suggesting the worst of the immediate pressure may have eased. Over the past week, however, the stock cratered on geopolitical concerns about Iran negotiations stalling and broader political headwinds: a Democratic midterm victory shifted momentum toward renewable energy policy, directly threatening the refining sector's long-term outlook.

The two-week decline reflects a collision of bad news for refiners. Stalled Iran talks raised Middle East tensions and oil supply uncertainty early in the period, while the midterm results and subsequent political messaging made clear that the new Congress will push harder on clean energy—a structural headwind for traditional oil refining demand over years to come. Today's recovery is a tactical bounce, not a reversal of that underlying concern.
